doc.title: Bill Goodwin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 28, 2025

title: What makes a good bass player
summary: Gilmore's electric and upright bass, and Goodwin's idea of a good bassist, with Gary Peacock, Red Mitchell and Leroy Vinnegar.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: He would from time to time.
He played the stand-up bass mostly but then he had the electric and he could play it very well.
A good bass player. They could be playing a washtub —
It doesn’t matter what he’s playing. Okay what makes a good bass player?
Well a beautiful time feeling that can negotiate the odd sensation of playing with me I think.

Somebody you can groove with. You know it’s nice to really work with some bass players. I could always play easily with Gary Peacock, Red Mitchell. We had to work at it for a while but we stuck with it and eventually became very good together. Then I fortuitously moved across the street from Leroy Vinnegar in the Hollywood Hills and he befriended me and then I played with his group. So I was always playing with really good bass players or as much as I could. But after I played with Leroy it’s like I could get that feeling without — the feeling I got with him I could get with other bass players, which is saying something because you know he was just such a rock, man, a wonderful beat. That’s always been the thing for me is the beat, the way the bass and drums combine, you know to me that’s like the beautiful part of the music. That feeling is very energizing.
